subject: miltiades
note: Miltiades, Cimonis filius, Atheniensis: an Athenian of ancient family.

subject: miltiades
note: Called at Lemnos en route and later subjected the island to Athens.

subject: miltiades
note: Ruled the Thracian Chersonese with quasi-regal authority.

subject: miltiades
note: Commanded the Athenians at the battle of Marathon against Datis.

subject: miltiades
note: Led the failed expedition against Paros, source of his condemnation.

subject: miltiades
note: Died in the public prison at Athens of the wound received at Paros.

subject: themistocles
note: Themistocles, Neocli filius, Atheniensis.

subject: themistocles
note: Engineered and fought the naval battle of Salamis.

subject: themistocles
note: Ostracized; withdrew to Argos, then fled via Corcyra to king Admetus when condemned in absence.

subject: themistocles
note: Fled to the Persian court and won the favor of Artaxerxes.

subject: themistocles
note: Given Magnesia by the king; settled there.

subject: themistocles
note: Died at Magnesia; Nepos reports both illness and the rumor of self-poisoning (reported assertion).

subject: aristides
note: Aristides, Lysimachi filius, Atheniensis.

subject: aristides
note: Ostracized for ten years' exile though famed for justice; recalled before the Persian invasion.

subject: aristides
note: Fought in the sea battle at Salamis before his recall from exile took effect.

subject: aristides
note: Athenian general at Plataea where Mardonius was routed.

subject: aristides
note: Died about four years after Themistocles' banishment, so poor he left scarcely enough for burial.

subject: pausanias
note: Pausanias Lacedaemonius: a Spartan of the royal house.

subject: pausanias
note: Commanded the Greeks when Mardonius was driven from Greece.

subject: pausanias
note: Took Byzantium and began his medizing correspondence with Xerxes.

subject: pausanias
note: Walled up in the temple of Athena of the Brazen House and starved.

subject: cimon
note: Cimon, Miltiadis filius, Atheniensis.

subject: cimon
note: Defeated the Thracians at the river Strymon and founded Amphipolis.

subject: cimon
note: Ostracized for ten years despite his services; recalled early.

subject: cimon
note: Died of illness while besieging Citium on Cyprus.

subject: lysander
note: Lysander Lacedaemonius.

subject: lysander
note: Destroyed the Athenian fleet at Aegospotami, ending the Peloponnesian War.

subject: lysander
note: Killed in battle at Haliartus in Boeotia.

subject: alcibiades
note: Alcibiades, Cliniae filius, Atheniensis.

subject: alcibiades
note: Chosen general for the Sicilian expedition, recalled to stand trial.

subject: alcibiades
note: Condemned in absence, took refuge at Sparta and advised Athens' enemies.

subject: alcibiades
note: Won victories at Cyzicus and on the Hellespont after joining the fleet.

subject: alcibiades
note: Withdrew to his castles in Thrace after his second fall.

subject: alcibiades
note: Burned to death in Phrygia through Pharnabazus' agents.

subject: thrasybulus
note: Thrasybulus, Lyci filius, Atheniensis.

subject: thrasybulus
note: From Phyle seized the Piraeus and overthrew the Thirty Tyrants.

subject: thrasybulus
note: Killed in his tent by barbarians after bringing his fleet to Cilicia.

subject: conon
note: Conon Atheniensis.

subject: conon
note: After Aegospotami betook himself to Pharnabazus, satrap of Ionia and Lydia, rather than return home.

subject: conon
note: Commanding the Persian fleet, crushed Sparta's sea power off Cnidus.

subject: conon
note: Returned in triumph and rebuilt the Long Walls of Athens.

subject: conon
note: Arrested by Tiribazus; Nepos leaves his end uncertain; he died on Cyprus by most accounts.

subject: dion
note: Dion, Hipparini filius, Syracusanus, nobili genere natus.

subject: dion
note: Banished by Dionysius II; lived in Greece, chiefly Corinth and Athens.

subject: dion
note: Sailed back and liberated Syracuse from the tyrant.

subject: dion
note: Assassinated in his own house by conspirators under Callicrates.

subject: iphicrates
note: Iphicrates Atheniensis: famed for discipline and the reformed peltast.

subject: iphicrates
note: Destroyed a Spartan mora near Corinth.

subject: iphicrates
note: Served Seuthes in Thrace and restored him to his kingdom.

subject: iphicrates
note: Acquitted at his capital trial, lived out his days at Athens.

subject: chabrias
note: Chabrias Atheniensis.

subject: chabrias
note: Commanded for Nectanebo in Egypt of his own accord.

subject: chabrias
note: Died fighting from his ship in the harbor of Chios in the Social War, refusing to abandon it.

subject: timotheus
note: Timotheus, Cononis filius, Atheniensis.

subject: timotheus
note: Circumnavigated the Peloponnese, defeating the Spartans off Corcyra.

subject: timotheus
note: Condemned in the Social War prosecution, withdrew to Chalcis.

subject: timotheus
note: Died in exile at Chalcis.

subject: datames
note: Patre Camisare, natione Care, matre Scythissa natus: of Carian stock.

subject: datames
note: Governed Cappadocia, inherited from his father.

subject: datames
note: Appointed to command the Egyptian expedition before the court turned against him.

subject: datames
note: Murdered at a parley by Mithridates after surviving many plots.

subject: epaminondas
note: Epaminondas, Polymnii filius, Thebanus.

subject: epaminondas
note: Broke Spartan power at Leuctra.

subject: epaminondas
note: Invaded the Peloponnese and marched to the gates of Sparta itself.

subject: epaminondas
note: Mortally wounded at Mantinea; died on hearing the Boeotians had won.

subject: pelopidas
note: Pelopidas Thebanus.

subject: pelopidas
note: Fled to Athens when the Spartans seized the Cadmea.

subject: pelopidas
note: Returned in disguise and liberated Thebes from the tyrants.

subject: pelopidas
note: Fell at Cynoscephalae in Thessaly charging Alexander of Pherae.

subject: agesilaus
note: Agesilaus Lacedaemonius, king of Sparta.

subject: agesilaus
note: Campaigned in Asia against Tissaphernes, outwitting his perjury.

subject: agesilaus
note: In old age served king Nectanebo in Egypt for pay.

subject: agesilaus
note: Died on the voyage home at the Harbor of Menelaus; his body was carried to Sparta in wax.

subject: eumenes
note: Eumenes Cardianus: a Greek among Macedonians, which always told against him.

subject: eumenes
note: Secretary and confidant of Philip and Alexander for twenty years.

subject: eumenes
note: Received Cappadocia in the division of the empire and made it his base.

subject: eumenes
note: Betrayed by the Silver Shields after Gabiene and killed in Antigonus' custody.

subject: phocion
note: Phocion Atheniensis: called The Good.

subject: phocion
note: Condemned by the restored democracy, drank the hemlock at eighty; buried at first outside Attica.

subject: timoleon
note: Timoleon Corinthius.

subject: timoleon
note: Sent to Sicily, expelled Dionysius, and refounded Syracuse.

subject: timoleon
note: Laid down power but remained at Syracuse, blind and revered, to the end.

subject: timoleon
note: Died at Syracuse and was buried at public expense.

subject: hamilcar
note: Hamilcar, cognomine Barca, Karthaginiensis.

subject: hamilcar
note: Commanded in Sicily at the end of the First Punic War, undefeated on Eryx.

subject: hamilcar
note: Crossed to Hispania with his army, and with the nine-year-old Hannibal.

subject: hamilcar
note: Fell in battle against the Vettones in Hispania.

subject: hannibal
note: Hannibal, Hamilcaris filius, Karthaginiensis.

subject: hannibal
note: Raised in his father's camp in Hispania; sworn eternal enmity to Rome at the altar.

subject: hannibal
note: Crossed the Alps into Italy; Cannae the greatest of his victories.

subject: hannibal
note: Recalled to Africa; defeated by Scipio near Zama.

subject: hannibal
note: Fled Carthage secretly by ship to Antiochus in Syria, then wandered court to court.

subject: hannibal
note: Took poison at Libyssa in Bithynia rather than be surrendered to Rome.

subject: cato
note: M. Cato, ortus municipio Tusculo.

subject: cato
note: Urged to Rome by L. Valerius Flaccus; rose through every office to the censorship.

subject: cato
note: As consul held Hispania Citerior and triumphed from it.

subject: cato
note: Died at eighty-five, still prosecuting and writing, the Origines in hand.

subject: atticus
note: T. Pomponius Atticus, ab origine ultima stirpis Romanae generatus.

subject: atticus
note: Removed to Athens during the civil strife; so beloved the city offered him citizenship.

subject: atticus
note: Kept his estate at Buthrotum in Epirus.

subject: atticus
note: Returned to Rome; friend of Cicero, Hortensius, and later Octavian, of no party.

subject: atticus
note: Facing incurable illness, ended his life by voluntary starvation at seventy-seven.

subject: cimon
note: Cimon, Miltiadis filius: son of Miltiades; paid his father's fine to recover his body for burial.

subject: hannibal
note: Hannibal, Hamilcaris filius: taken to Hispania at nine and sworn at his father's altar to eternal enmity with Rome.

subject: timotheus
note: Timotheus, Cononis filius: added his own glory to the fame inherited from his father.

subject: apollocrates
note: In the peace pact Syracuse was to go to Apollocrates, 'cui maximam fidem uni habebat': the one man Dionysius trusted most: his eldest son, left in charge of the citadel.

subject: dionysius-i
note: Dionysius the Elder married Aristomache, Dion's sister ('Dionysius prior ... Aristomachen, sororem Dionis, duxit uxorem'), binding Dion into the tyrant's house.

subject: dionysius-i
note: By Aristomache Dionysius the Elder had two daughters, Sophrosyne and Arete; Sophrosyne he gave in marriage to his son Dionysius, the younger tyrant who succeeded him.

subject: dion
note: Dionysius the Elder gave his daughter Arete, Dion's own niece by Aristomache, to Dion in marriage: 'alteram, Areten, Dioni'.

subject: aristomache
note: 'Dionysius prior ... Aristomachen, sororem Dionis, duxit uxorem': Dionysius the Elder married Aristomache, Dion's sister.

subject: aristomache
note: Aristomache was Dion's sister ('Aristomachen, sororem Dionis'), the marriage that bound Dion into the tyrant's house.

subject: sophrosyne
note: By Aristomache Dionysius the Elder had two daughters, Sophrosyne and Arete: 'ex qua duas filias habuit, Sophrosynen et Areten'.

subject: sophrosyne
note: Sophrosyne was given in marriage to Dionysius the Younger ('quarum priorem Dionysio filio ... conlocavit'), wedding half-siblings within the tyrant's house.

subject: arete
note: Arete was the second daughter of Dionysius the Elder by Aristomache: 'ex qua duas filias habuit, Sophrosynen et Areten'.

subject: arete
note: Dionysius gave Arete, Dion's own niece by Aristomache, to Dion in marriage: 'alteram, Areten, Dioni'.

subject: apollocrates
note: Held the citadel and island quarter of Syracuse for the tyrant's house while Dion controlled the rest of the city.

subject: dion
note: Within three days of reaching Sicily Dion took Syracuse, broke the fifty-year tyranny, and drove Dionysius II from all but the citadel; by the pact Dionysius withdrew to Italy.

subject: themistocles
note: Rivals for the leadership of Athens; Aristides was ostracized largely through the faction of Themistocles.

subject: aristides
note: Shared the command with Pausanias in the campaign that drove Mardonius from Greece; under him the naval hegemony passed to Athens.

subject: themistocles
note: When Pausanias' treasonous letters were discovered, the Spartans alleged Themistocles shared his medizing designs (reported assertion).

subject: alcibiades
note: Joined Thrasybulus' fleet and with him won the victories at Cyzicus and on the Hellespont.

subject: lysander
note: Alcibiades warned the Athenian generals before Aegospotami; ignored, they lost the fleet to Lysander.

subject: lysander
note: Through Lysander's backing Agesilaus obtained the kingship over Leotychides.

subject: conon
note: Conon's victory at Cnidus with the Persian fleet undid the Spartan sea power Agesilaus fought to sustain in Asia.

subject: epaminondas
note: The closest of colleagues; together they liberated Thebes and broke the power of Sparta.

subject: epaminondas
note: Marched to the gates of Sparta itself; Agesilaus' defense of the city checked him.

subject: iphicrates
note: Prosecuted together after the Social War; Iphicrates was acquitted, Timotheus condemned.

subject: chabrias
note: Fellow Athenian commanders of the same generation, entangled in the same Social War.

subject: iphicrates
note: The great Athenian captains of the age between Conon and Phocion, named together by Nepos.

subject: chabrias
note: Both served the Egyptian kings for pay: Chabrias of his own accord, Agesilaus by public commission.

subject: dion
note: Dion first broke the tyranny at Syracuse; a decade later Timoleon expelled Dionysius for good and refounded the city.

subject: cato
note: Cato served as military tribune in the war against Hannibal, the enemy whose defeat shaped his whole politics.

subject: miltiades
note: Marathon and Salamis: the two deliverances of Greece, one generation apart, joined by Nepos' own comparison.

subject: agesilaus
note: Made king of Sparta over Leotychides, through the influence of Lysander.

subject: cato
note: Rose through every magistracy: consul with Flaccus, and censor of proverbial severity.

subject: phocion
note: Held the Athenian generalship forty-five times without ever canvassing for it.

subject: hannibal
note: Commander-in-chief of the Carthaginian armies at twenty-five; later chosen king (suffete) at home.

subject: eumenes
note: Secretary (scriba) to Philip and to Alexander, an office of honor among Greeks, held for twenty years.

subject: pausanias
note: Regent of Sparta and commander of the allied Greeks after the Persian invasion.
